about.title: Cupertino Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Cupertino residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Santa Clara County medical systems, and most visits go the way they should. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgical step is skipped, or medication is mismanaged, the resulting harm can be serious and lasting. California treats these cases differently than an ordinary injury claim — a bad result by itself doesn't establish fault, and the law requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in before a case can move forward. There's also a 90-day notice requirement before a lawsuit can be filed, and the filing window is generally one year from when the harm is discovered, capped at three years from the injury itself. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take on cases directly. Instead, we connect Cupertino residents who believe they were harmed by substandard medical care with an independent attorney experienced in these specific rules, so you don't have to sort them out alone.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: The Clock Starts Sooner Than You Think
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discover the harm, but no more than three years from the injury, so waiting can quietly close the door on a claim.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed, California requires a formal 90-day notice to the provider, a step an attorney can help prepare correctly.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone isn't proof of negligence, these cases typically need a qualified medical expert to establish what went wrong and why.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every complication or disappointing result is caused by negligence. An attorney working with a qualified medical expert can help determine whether the care fell below the accepted standard.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a claim in Cupertino?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from when it happened. There's also a required 90-day pre-suit notice, so it's wise to speak with someone well before any deadline approaches.

items.question: Are there limits on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are generally not subject to that same cap, and an independent attorney can walk through how this applies to your situation.

items.question: Do I need to have been treated at a specific Cupertino facility to qualify for help?
items.answer: No. Whether your care happened at a local clinic, a larger Santa Clara County hospital system, or elsewhere, LawProactive can help connect you with an attorney who handles these claims regardless of the specific facility involved.
